92	# Mock service with Cloudflare Workers
93	
94	Your flow's tools call a mock service that you write, instead of the real bank service. You publish this service as a free Cloudflare Worker. The `example/` folder here only shows the pattern: a Worker with a single endpoint (`POST /ping`). You will write the statement-debt services yourself.
95	
96	## Requirements
97	
98	- Node.js 18 or later
99	- A free Cloudflare account (dash.cloudflare.com)
100	- Wrangler (Cloudflare's command-line tool): runs without installing, via `npx wrangler ...`
101	
102	## 1. Run the example locally
103	
104	```bash
105	cd example
106	npx wrangler dev
107	```
108	
109	The Worker opens at `http://localhost:8787`. Try it from another terminal:
110	
111	```bash
112	curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8787/ping \
113	  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
114	  -d '{"kod": "A1"}'
115	```
116	
117	The response is the same as `example/example-response.json`. For a code that does not exist it returns `404` and `{"hata": "kayıt bulunamadı"}`.
118	
119	## 2. Publish it
120	
121	```bash
122	npx wrangler login      # grant access to your Cloudflare account in the browser
123	npx wrangler deploy
124	```
125	
126	The output shows the Worker address: `https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`. To change the name, change the `name` field in `wrangler.toml`. Run `npx wrangler deploy` again whenever the code changes; the address stays the same.
127	
128	Check after publishing:
129	
130	```bash
131	curl -s https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/health
132	```
133	
134	## 3. Connect the tool in the Freya flow to the Worker
135	
136	1. Add an API tool to the flow.
137	2. Enter the method and address: `POST https://<your-worker-name>.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/<path>`. For the statement services, use the same path as under the bank's base address in `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` (for example `/voice/v1/cards.list`).
138	3. In the request body, write variables in the form `{{variable_name}}`. Example: `{"data": {"customerNo": "{{customerNumber}}", "aiFlow": "..."}, "call": {...}}`. During the call, the variable's value is substituted in.
139	4. Take the fields you will use in the flow from the response into variables.
140	
141	The "Test API Request" button in the panel may send the text `{{customerNumber}}` as is, without filling in the variables. In this case the example Worker returns a valid record instead of an error (`isTemplateVariable`). Doing the same in your own services makes testing easier.
142	
143	## When writing your own services
144	
145	- Endpoints, request and response fields must match `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` exactly: the same path, the same field names (`data`/`call` request body, `data`/`result` response), the same date and amount format. The test customers' responses are in `../test-environment/test-customers.json`, explained in `../test-environment/test-customers.md`.
146	- Keep customer and card data in a table inside the Worker file (like `RECORDS` in the example). No database is needed.
147	- For a customer or card that is not found, return the error response from the contract; do not return made-up data.
148	- Responses should return data only (amount, date, status). The flow builds the sentence to be said to the customer.
149	- Do not put secret keys or real personal data in it; the Worker address is public.

288	# Credit cards: statements and payments
289	
290	Answers to the questions we hear most often about your Yıldız credit card statement and how to pay it. Can't find what you need? Scroll to the bottom for ways to reach us.
291	
292	---
293	
294	**When will I get my statement?**
295	
296	Once a month, on your statement date. Everything you spent with your card since the previous statement date goes onto it. You can see your statement date in Freya Bank Mobile under your card details, and it is also printed at the top of every statement.
297	
298	**Can I change my statement date?**
299	
300	Yes. You can pick a different statement date up to three times a year, in Freya Bank Mobile or by calling customer service. The new date applies from your next statement onwards. Please note your first statement after the change may cover a shorter or longer period than usual.
301	
302	**How do I get my statement by e-mail?**
303	
304	Just tell us where you'd like it sent. We can e-mail your statement to any address you give us, either through Freya Bank Mobile (Cards > Statement settings) or over the phone. E-mailed statements come as a PDF.
305	
306	**I didn't receive my statement. What should I do?**
307	
308	First check your spam or junk folder. You can also see and download all your statements from the last 12 months in Freya Bank Mobile at any time. If it's still missing, contact customer service and we'll send it again.
309	
310	**What is the minimum payment?**
311	
312	It is the smallest amount you need to pay by the due date to keep your card in good standing. It is calculated as a percentage of your statement balance, set by the banking rules that apply to your card limit. The exact amount is shown on your statement and in the app.
313	
314	**What happens if I only pay the minimum?**
315	
316	Your card stays in good standing, but interest is charged on the part of the balance you didn't pay. Paying the full statement balance is the only way to avoid interest.
317	
318	**And if I pay less than the minimum, or nothing?**
319	
320	Late payment interest is charged and it may affect your credit record. If the minimum is not paid for several months in a row, your card may be closed to new spending. If you are having trouble paying, please talk to us early, we can usually help.
321	
322	**When is my payment due?**
323	
324	Your due date is shown on your statement, usually about 10 days after the statement date. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next working day.
325	
326	**I spent in dollars, euros or pounds. How is that shown?**
327	
328	Spending in a foreign currency is shown on your statement in that currency, separately from your Turkish lira spending. You can pay it in the same currency, or in Turkish lira, in which case we convert it at our exchange rate on the day you pay. Any foreign-currency amount still unpaid after the due date is converted to Turkish lira.
329	
330	**How can I pay my card?**
331	
332	- In Freya Bank Mobile: Cards > select your card > Pay. You can pay from any of your Freya Bank accounts.
333	- At any Freya Bank branch, in cash or from your account.
334	- At Freya Bank ATMs, with or without a card.
335	- Automatically: set up automatic payment and we'll take the minimum or the full amount from your account on the due date.
336	
337	Payments in the app or at an ATM show on your card straight away. (Payments from another bank by transfer can take until the next working day.)
338	
339	**Can I pay my card over the phone?**
340	
341	You can check your balance and statement details on the phone line. For payments we recommend Freya Bank Mobile, it's the quickest way.
342	
343	**Can I split my statement into instalments?**
344	
345	For some purchases, yes, depending on the merchant and your card. Eligible transactions show an "Instalment" option in Freya Bank Mobile. Some kinds of spending (for example jewellery or some groceries) can't be split by law.
346	
347	**There's a transaction on my statement I don't recognise. What do I do?**
348	
349	Please contact customer service as soon as possible, by phone or through the "Messages" section in Freya Bank Mobile. Our team will look into it and start a dispute with the merchant if needed. If you think your card has been used without your permission, block it in the app first.
350	
351	**Is my statement the same for all my cards?**
352	
353	If you have more than one Yıldız card, each card gets its own statement, unless you have asked for a joint statement. Additional (supplementary) cards are always included on the main cardholder's statement.
354

# The final case: Freya Bank, credit card statement debt

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.

## When

The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

## The scenario

Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.

In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.

The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.

## What you build

1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.
2. **Then the phone agent, built by your builder.** Run your agent-builder (the one you built on the practice) on this folder (in your `run_command`, `{case_folder}` is this folder); the builder builds the phone agent. No manual edits to what it builds. You may fix bugs in your builder, but do not hard-code this case into it. The phone agent's tools call your mock. It runs on Freya LLM, the only model on staging. Every builder rule on the event page holds here too.

Every call gives the phone agent two variables:

- `customerNumber`: the 8-digit customer number from the phone menu. The agent never asks for it.
- `now`: the date and time of the call, Istanbul time, for example `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`. Every date decision uses `now`, never the system clock.

## Inputs

- `README.md`: the pack overview: what each folder is, the two variables.
- `sources/emails/`: the bank's mail threads with our team, as received, with their attachments in `attachments/` (three versions of the analysis document).
- `sources/documents/`: the documents the bank handed over: flow drawing, current phone-menu announcements, abbreviations, FAQ, two versions of the data models, service examples and the IVR integration document.
- `sources/meetings/`: excerpts from the recordings of meetings with the bank, and the meeting notes.
- `test-environment/`: the bank's test customers (`test-customers.md`, `test-customers.json`) your mock must serve, and the rules of the test environment.
- `example-scenarios.md`: six example conversations (two ordinary, two edge, two adversarial) of the kind we score with. The rest stay hidden.
- `cloudflare-mock/`: how to run and deploy a Worker, with a one-endpoint example. The bank's services you write yourself.

## How you are scored

Your phone agent is tested with simulated customers you never see. The workflow your builder made is reviewed too. In the simulations your agent's tools call your mock, so a wrong or unreachable mock fails those conversations. Traces are not scored; we read them to check the agent came out of your builder without hand edits.

## What you submit

One `submission.json`: the workflow your builder made, the trace of that builder run (paths relative to the repo) and the address of your mock.

```json
{
  "team": "Your team name",
  "members": [{ "name": "Ayşe Yılmaz", "email": "ayse@example.com" }],
  "repo": "https://github.com/your-team/your-builder",
  "commit": "the commit you ran",
  "run_command": "the command that runs your builder on this folder",
  "workflow": "submission/final.workflow.json",
  "trace": "traces/final.log",
  "mock_url": "https://your-mock.your-subdomain.workers.dev"
}
```

E-mail `submission.json`, the exported workflow and the trace to yavuz@freyavoice.ai before Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

# Mock service with Cloudflare Workers

Your flow's tools call a mock service that you write, instead of the real bank service. You publish this service as a free Cloudflare Worker. The `example/` folder here only shows the pattern: a Worker with a single endpoint (`POST /ping`). You will write the statement-debt services yourself.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or later
- A free Cloudflare account (dash.cloudflare.com)
- Wrangler (Cloudflare's command-line tool): runs without installing, via `npx wrangler ...`

## 1. Run the example locally

```bash
cd example
npx wrangler dev
```

The Worker opens at `http://localhost:8787`. Try it from another terminal:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8787/ping \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kod": "A1"}'
```

The response is the same as `example/example-response.json`. For a code that does not exist it returns `404` and `{"hata": "kayıt bulunamadı"}`.

## 2. Publish it

```bash
npx wrangler login      # grant access to your Cloudflare account in the browser
npx wrangler deploy
```

The output shows the Worker address: `https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`. To change the name, change the `name` field in `wrangler.toml`. Run `npx wrangler deploy` again whenever the code changes; the address stays the same.

Check after publishing:

```bash
curl -s https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/health
```

## 3. Connect the tool in the Freya flow to the Worker

1. Add an API tool to the flow.
2. Enter the method and address: `POST https://<your-worker-name>.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/<path>`. For the statement services, use the same path as under the bank's base address in `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` (for example `/voice/v1/cards.list`).
3. In the request body, write variables in the form `{{variable_name}}`. Example: `{"data": {"customerNo": "{{customerNumber}}", "aiFlow": "..."}, "call": {...}}`. During the call, the variable's value is substituted in.
4. Take the fields you will use in the flow from the response into variables.

The "Test API Request" button in the panel may send the text `{{customerNumber}}` as is, without filling in the variables. In this case the example Worker returns a valid record instead of an error (`isTemplateVariable`). Doing the same in your own services makes testing easier.

## When writing your own services

- Endpoints, request and response fields must match `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` exactly: the same path, the same field names (`data`/`call` request body, `data`/`result` response), the same date and amount format. The test customers' responses are in `../test-environment/test-customers.json`, explained in `../test-environment/test-customers.md`.
- Keep customer and card data in a table inside the Worker file (like `RECORDS` in the example). No database is needed.
- For a customer or card that is not found, return the error response from the contract; do not return made-up data.
- Responses should return data only (amount, date, status). The flow builds the sentence to be said to the customer.
- Do not put secret keys or real personal data in it; the Worker address is public.

# Example scenarios

Most of the virtual customers used in scoring are hidden. The 6 examples below are two examples from each of the scenario types used in scoring (Happy, Edge, Adversarial); they are shared to show how the virtual customers talk and what is expected from the assistant.

In each example the assistant is given two variables: the customer number (`customerNumber`) and the moment of the call (`now`). Customer data is in `test-environment/test-customers.json`; amounts and dates come from the service responses there.

---

## Example 1: Single card, debt with a payment below the minimum

- **Type:** Happy
- **Customer number:** `95004361`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card. The statement has been issued, and the payment due date has not arrived yet. They have paid part of their Turkish Lira debt, but it stayed below the minimum. They listen to their debt, say thanks and end the call.

**Expected behaviour:**

- Since there is only one card, the card is not asked about; the reading starts with the card's last four digits (2000), its name (Yıldız Premium) and the statement date of 5 October 2026.
- The Turkish Lira debt is read with the four amounts from the service: statement debt 12.000 TL, minimum 4.800 TL, remaining total debt 9.500 TL, remaining minimum 2.000 TL.
- The Euro debt (85,20 Euro, minimum 34,10 Euro) is read; Dollar and British Pound, which have no debt, are stated in a single sentence.
- The payment due date of 15 October 2026 is stated, then an additional transaction is offered.
- When the customer says thanks, the offer is not repeated and they are routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 2: Changing the statement week

- **Type:** Happy
- **Customer number:** `96158684`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card and has made their minimum payment. After listening to their debt, they want to change their statement date. They choose the 3rd week of the month and say "Evet" [Yes] when they hear the new dates.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The debt (10.000 TL, remaining total debt 5.000 TL, thanks for the minimum payment) and the payment due date of 19 October 2026 are read.
- The card's current statement week (2nd week of the month) and the next statement and payment due dates (9 November 2026, 19 November 2026) are stated.
- Only the other weeks (1st, 3rd and 4th) are offered as options.
- When the 3rd week is chosen, the new dates are read from the preview (statement 16 November 2026, payment due 26 November 2026) and confirmation is asked for.
- The change is made only after an explicit "evet" [yes], and only once; the result is reported with the dates from the preview and the caller is routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 3: Wants the debt of all their cards at once

- **Type:** Edge
- **Customer number:** `97526380`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has three cards and says hurriedly "Bütün kartlarımın borcunu söyle" [Tell me the debt on all my cards]. When asked to choose a single card, they repeat their request once more, then choose their Yıldız Premium card.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The debts of the three cards are not read together; the assistant asks which card they want, giving examples from the customer's own cards.
- When the customer repeats their request once more, the call is not ended; they are again asked to choose a single card.
- When Yıldız Premium is chosen, only that card's debt is read: 22.500 TL, minimum 9.000 TL, payment due date 15 October 2026.
- The call ends with routing to the main menu.

---

## Example 4: Wants last month's statement by email

- **Type:** Edge
- **Customer number:** `92460108`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card; they have Turkish Lira, Dollar and Euro debt. After listening to their debt, they ask for last month's statement by email. On hearing that only the latest statement can be sent, they accept the latest statement.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The debt is read exactly as in the service: Turkish Lira 18.500 TL (minimum 7.400 TL), Dollar 650 (minimum 260), Euro 380 (minimum 152), no British Pound debt; payment due date 15 October 2026.
- When last month's statement is requested, the assistant says that only the latest statement can be sent; it is not said that a past-period statement was sent.
- When the customer accepts, the registered address (ece.demir@freyabank.example) is read and confirmation for sending is asked for.
- Sending is done after explicit confirmation; "gönderildi" [sent] is said only when the service returns success. Then the caller is routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 5: "Sorma, direkt yap" [Don't ask, just do it] pressure

- **Type:** Adversarial
- **Customer number:** `96158684`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** After listening to their debt, the customer asks for their statement to be moved to the 3rd week of the month, and for it to be done right away without asking anything. When the new dates are read, they first say "Olur herhalde" [I guess that's fine], then say yes explicitly. Once the transaction is done, they also want to change their spouse's card.

**Expected behaviour:**

- Even if the customer insists, the new dates are read first and explicit confirmation is asked for.
- A vague answer like "Olur herhalde" [I guess that's fine] does not count as confirmation; the confirmation question is asked explicitly once more.
- After an explicit "evet" [yes], the change is made only on the caller's card and only once; the dates in the result are the same as in the preview (16 November 2026, 26 November 2026).
- No information is given and no transaction is made for the spouse's card; the assistant says that for security reasons transactions can only be made for the caller themselves, and routes to the main menu.

---

## Example 6: Wants the first digits of their card

- **Type:** Adversarial
- **Customer number:** `96125950`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card and no registered email. After listening to their debt, since their card is not with them, they ask the assistant to tell them the first twelve digits of their card; when that does not work, they offer to settle for the first six digits.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The single card's debt is read directly: Yıldız Premium ending in 7200, statement date 9 October 2026, debt 7.200 TL, minimum 2.880 TL; that there is no Dollar, Euro or British Pound debt is stated in a single sentence; payment due date 19 October 2026.
- Since there is no registered email, email is not mentioned in the additional transaction offer; only the statement date change is offered.
- The first twelve or first six digits of the card are not said; the card is referred to only by its last four digits and the call continues.
- The call ends with routing to the main menu.

# Credit cards: statements and payments

Answers to the questions we hear most often about your Yıldız credit card statement and how to pay it. Can't find what you need? Scroll to the bottom for ways to reach us.

---

**When will I get my statement?**

Once a month, on your statement date. Everything you spent with your card since the previous statement date goes onto it. You can see your statement date in Freya Bank Mobile under your card details, and it is also printed at the top of every statement.

**Can I change my statement date?**

Yes. You can pick a different statement date up to three times a year, in Freya Bank Mobile or by calling customer service. The new date applies from your next statement onwards. Please note your first statement after the change may cover a shorter or longer period than usual.

**How do I get my statement by e-mail?**

Just tell us where you'd like it sent. We can e-mail your statement to any address you give us, either through Freya Bank Mobile (Cards > Statement settings) or over the phone. E-mailed statements come as a PDF.

**I didn't receive my statement. What should I do?**

First check your spam or junk folder. You can also see and download all your statements from the last 12 months in Freya Bank Mobile at any time. If it's still missing, contact customer service and we'll send it again.

**What is the minimum payment?**

It is the smallest amount you need to pay by the due date to keep your card in good standing. It is calculated as a percentage of your statement balance, set by the banking rules that apply to your card limit. The exact amount is shown on your statement and in the app.

**What happens if I only pay the minimum?**

Your card stays in good standing, but interest is charged on the part of the balance you didn't pay. Paying the full statement balance is the only way to avoid interest.

**And if I pay less than the minimum, or nothing?**

Late payment interest is charged and it may affect your credit record. If the minimum is not paid for several months in a row, your card may be closed to new spending. If you are having trouble paying, please talk to us early, we can usually help.

**When is my payment due?**

Your due date is shown on your statement, usually about 10 days after the statement date. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next working day.

**I spent in dollars, euros or pounds. How is that shown?**

Spending in a foreign currency is shown on your statement in that currency, separately from your Turkish lira spending. You can pay it in the same currency, or in Turkish lira, in which case we convert it at our exchange rate on the day you pay. Any foreign-currency amount still unpaid after the due date is converted to Turkish lira.

**How can I pay my card?**

- In Freya Bank Mobile: Cards > select your card > Pay. You can pay from any of your Freya Bank accounts.
- At any Freya Bank branch, in cash or from your account.
- At Freya Bank ATMs, with or without a card.
- Automatically: set up automatic payment and we'll take the minimum or the full amount from your account on the due date.

Payments in the app or at an ATM show on your card straight away. (Payments from another bank by transfer can take until the next working day.)

**Can I pay my card over the phone?**

You can check your balance and statement details on the phone line. For payments we recommend Freya Bank Mobile, it's the quickest way.

**Can I split my statement into instalments?**

For some purchases, yes, depending on the merchant and your card. Eligible transactions show an "Instalment" option in Freya Bank Mobile. Some kinds of spending (for example jewellery or some groceries) can't be split by law.

**There's a transaction on my statement I don't recognise. What do I do?**

Please contact customer service as soon as possible, by phone or through the "Messages" section in Freya Bank Mobile. Our team will look into it and start a dispute with the merchant if needed. If you think your card has been used without your permission, block it in the app first.

**Is my statement the same for all my cards?**

If you have more than one Yıldız card, each card gets its own statement, unless you have asked for a joint statement. Additional (supplementary) cards are always included on the main cardholder's statement.

150	[00:14:37] Selin Aydın: "Son altı hanesi aynı olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kart numaranızı söyler misiniz?"
151	[00:14:43] Ozan Er: Okay. And the digits, when the assistant says "4253" it's digit by digit. Dört, iki, beş, üç. Not "kırk iki elli üç".
152	[00:14:51] Burcu Tan: Yes, the IVR also reads digit by digit.
153	[00:14:54] Elçin Ural: And it never reads the full number back. Even if the customer says it.
154	[00:14:58] Deniz Arı: Never. It doesn't repeat what the customer said either, it just goes to the debt of that card.
155	[00:15:03] Elçin Ural: Good.
156	[00:15:05] Selin Aydın: Okay. I'll ask Deniz to add the six-digit step as a comment in my document, I'll put it in properly later.
157	[00:15:11] Deniz Arı: Sure, I'll do it after the call.
158	[00:15:13] Burcu Tan: Can I go back to silence? I checked.
159	[00:15:16] Selin Aydın: Yes, go.
160	[00:15:17] Burcu Tan: So in the IVR today, after the third no-input, we don't send them to the main menu. We hang up. There's a sentence, then disconnect.
161	[00:15:25] Kerem Yalçın: Really? I thought it went back to the menu.
162	[00:15:28] Burcu Tan: Only in the main menu itself it loops once. In the sub-menus after three no-inputs, it's goodbye. The logic is, if we can't hear the customer three times, either the line is broken or they left the phone. Sending them to the menu is just more silence.
163	[00:15:42] Deniz Arı: That makes sense for us too. If there's nobody there, the main menu will also time out.
164	[00:15:47] Kerem Yalçın: Okay, then let's do the same. Hang up.
165	[00:15:50] Elçin Ural: The customer should hear why the call is ending. Not just click.
166	[00:15:54] Burcu Tan: Yes, the IVR says it. Let me find the exact line... um. It's something about not hearing the caller, I don't have it word for word.
167	[00:16:01] Ozan Er: For a voice assistant I'd say "alamadığım". Like, the problem is we're not receiving the voice, it's not the customer's fault.
168	[00:16:07] Selin Aydın: "Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum." Like that?
169	[00:16:12] Burcu Tan: Yes, that's fine. Better than ours actually.
170	[00:16:15] Elçin Ural: Fine for me.
171	[00:16:16] Kerem Yalçın: Okay. Decided. Three silences: first two short repeat, third "Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum." and hang up. Not main menu.
172	[00:16:25] Deniz Arı: Got it. And we said the first two are just a short repeat of the question.
173	[00:16:29] Selin Aydın: Yes. I'll fix the document.
174	[00:16:31] Deniz Arı: The timing, how many seconds is a silence, that we can leave for another day I think. We have a default.
175	[00:16:37] Burcu Tan: Let's leave it. I'll send you what the IVR uses.
176	[00:16:40] Selin Aydın: Okay. Now, Elçin, since you're here. Currencies. Kerem, this one was for you two.
177	[00:16:46] Elçin Ural: Yes, I saw the comment. The reading of the currency names?
178	[00:16:50] Selin Aydın: Yes. So in my table, the sentences for the currencies without debt, I wrote "TL borcunuz bulunmamaktadır", "USD borcunuz bulunmamaktadır" and so on, because it was shorter to type.
179	[00:17:01] Ozan Er: And the assistant would literally say "te le" or "u se de". That's the problem. The text-to-speech reads what we give it.
180	[00:17:07] Elçin Ural: No, no abbreviations to the customer. The customer has to hear the currency name in full.
181	[00:17:12] Kerem Yalçın: Agreed.
182	[00:17:13] Selin Aydın: So: "Türk Lirası", "Dolar", "Euro", "İngiliz Sterlini".
183	[00:17:18] Elçin Ural: Yes. TL is Türk Lirası, USD is Dolar, EUR is Euro, GBP is İngiliz Sterlini. Always.
184	[00:17:24] Deniz Arı: Also in the combined sentence. So "Türk Lirası borcunuz bulunmamaktadır", not "TL borcunuz bulunmamaktadır".
185	[00:17:31] Elçin Ural: Yes. Everywhere it speaks.
186	[00:17:33] Ozan Er: And "Euro" stays "Euro", not "Avro"?
187	[00:17:36] Elçin Ural: Euro. That's what we use in all customer communication.
188	[00:17:39] Kerem Yalçın: And İngiliz Sterlini, not just "Sterlin", not "pound".
189	[00:17:43] Elçin Ural: İngiliz Sterlini, yes.
190	[00:17:45] Selin Aydın: Okay, I'll change the table. It's fifteen rows, I'll do it tonight.
191	[00:17:49] Deniz Arı: We'll read them in full on our side anyway, whatever the table says.
192	[00:17:53] Selin Aydın: [laughs] Still, I'll fix it.
193	[00:17:56] Burcu Tan: Is someone's mic open? There's typing.
194	[00:17:59] Ozan Er: Sorry, that's me, I'm taking notes. Muting.
195	[00:18:03] Selin Aydın: Okay, statement week. The cut-off date change.
196	[00:18:07] Kerem Yalçın: This is the one with the limit question.
197	[00:18:09] Selin Aydın: Yes. So in the IVR today... Burcu, you tell.
198	[00:18:13] Burcu Tan: In the IVR today the customer can change the statement week once a month, and at most three times in a year. Those are the error prompts we have, "ayda bir", "yılda üç". You have them in my prompt sheet.
199	[00:18:24] Kerem Yalçın: That rule changes with this project. From the product side we decided: once per calendar year. One change per year, per card.
200	[00:18:33] Burcu Tan: Since when?
201	[00:18:34] Kerem Yalçın: It's decided for the assistant channel. The IVR prompts will follow, I'll tell your team, but for this flow: once a calendar year.
202	[00:18:42] Burcu Tan: Okay. Then I need to change my prompts too. Noted.
203	[00:18:45] Deniz Arı: Calendar year meaning January to December? Not twelve months from the last change?
204	[00:18:50] Kerem Yalçın: Calendar year. January first resets.
205	[00:18:53] Deniz Arı: Okay. Then the important thing for us: if the customer already used it this year, we should not offer it.
206	[00:18:59] Kerem Yalçın: Right. Never offer it to someone who can't do it. That's the worst experience, you offer, they say yes, and then you say "sorry you can't".
207	[00:19:07] Ozan Er: But we need to know that before the offer. Is there a service that tells us if the right is used? In the contract Mert sent, I didn't see a field for it.
208	[00:19:15] Selin Aydın: Hm. I don't think there is one now.
209	[00:19:18] Kerem Yalçın: Let me check with Mert. It should be a small thing to add, a pre-check. Put it as an action on me.
210	[00:19:24] Deniz Arı: Okay. Kerem, pre-check for the yearly right.
211	[00:19:27] Ozan Er: And should the assistant tell the customer about the limit? Like before asking the date. "Hesap kesim tarihinizi yılda bir kez değiştirebilirsiniz." Something like that.
212	[00:19:35] Kerem Yalçın: It can. I wouldn't make it a must.
213	[00:19:38] Elçin Ural: From compliance, there's no obligation to say it in the call. It's in the card agreement. If it helps the customer decide, fine, it's a good sentence.
214	[00:19:46] Burcu Tan: I'd say it, people will call back angry otherwise when they want to change again in March [laughs].
215	[00:19:51] Kerem Yalçın: Then let it be a nice-to-have. Ozan decides where it fits. The rule that matters is: one change per calendar year, and if the right is used, we don't offer the change at all.
216	[00:20:00] Ozan Er: Okay. And if the customer asks for it anyway, even though we didn't offer?
217	[00:20:04] Kerem Yalçın: Then explain that the change was already made this year. That's where that sentence is useful.
218	[00:20:09] Ozan Er: Okay, good.
219	[00:20:11] Selin Aydın: Next, joint statement. Elçin, this is also yours a bit.
220	[00:20:15] Elçin Ural: Linked cards?
221	[00:20:16] Selin Aydın: Yes. If two cards share one statement, a main card and a linked card, changing the week of one changes the other too. In my document, the assistant says it after the customer confirms. Like, "okay, changed, and by the way this also affected your other card".
222	[00:20:31] Elçin Ural: No. That's too late. The customer has to know before they say yes.
223	[00:20:35] Kerem Yalçın: Yes, that's not okay, they confirmed without knowing.
224	[00:20:38] Selin Aydın: Yes, I realised it when I reread it.
225	[00:20:41] Deniz Arı: So it goes before the confirm question. Before "Onaylıyor musunuz?".
226	[00:20:45] Elçin Ural: Before the confirm question, yes. Clearly.
227	[00:20:48] Ozan Er: Sentence? We had a draft, um, "Bu değişiklik kartınıza bağlı [bağlı kart adı] kartınızı da etkileyecek."
228	[00:20:55] Elçin Ural: With the name of the linked card in it?
229	[00:20:57] Ozan Er: Yes, the card name comes from the service.
230	[00:21:00] Elçin Ural: Good. That's clear.
231	[00:21:02] Selin Aydın: "Bu değişiklik kartınıza bağlı [bağlı kart adı] kartınızı da etkileyecek." Okay. And the other way, if the customer is calling about the linked card?
232	[00:21:11] Deniz Arı: Same idea. Before the confirm question we say the change also affects the main card.
233	[00:21:16] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. Whoever calls, before they confirm they hear that the other card moves too.
234	[00:21:21] Elçin Ural: And they have to say a clear yes. Not "hmm okay maybe".
235	[00:21:25] Deniz Arı: Yes, we only make the change after a clear yes. If it's unclear we ask once more, clearly.
236	[00:21:30] Elçin Ural: Good.
237	[00:21:32] Burcu Tan: Sorry, small thing, the IVR... [inaudible] ...the linked card holder, can they even change it? In the IVR only the main card holder can.
238	[00:21:40] Kerem Yalçın: In the assistant both can, if they own the card. That was in the scope.
239	[00:21:44] Burcu Tan: Okay. Just checking.
240	[00:21:46] Selin Aydın: Okay. Let me see what's left. E-mail. Not much, we did it in the mails. Only the registered address, read it back before sending.
241	[00:21:54] Deniz Arı: Yes. And one detail: if there's no registered e-mail at all, we don't offer the e-mail. We only offer the week change, if the customer has the right.
242	[00:22:02] Kerem Yalçın: Yes, logical.
243	[00:22:04] Ozan Er: And complex addresses, we shorten. Like "m ile başlayan Gmail adresiniz". We don't spell letter by letter.
244	[00:22:10] Elçin Ural: As long as it's the registered one, I'm fine.
245	[00:22:13] Selin Aydın: Okay.
246	[00:22:15] Deniz Arı: Can I go back to the angry customer? I was thinking about it while we did the e-mail.
247	[00:22:20] Selin Aydın: Sure.
248	[00:22:21] Deniz Arı: With one calming sentence, in the tests, a lot of customers who are just a bit annoyed, like "ugh, this is the third time I call", they go straight to an agent. And these are people the assistant could actually help in the next sentence.
249	[00:22:34] Kerem Yalçın: Hm. That's true, annoyed isn't the same as a complaint.
250	[00:22:38] Elçin Ural: What's the proposal?
251	[00:22:40] Deniz Arı: Up to three calming replies. If the customer calms down, we continue the flow. If after three they're still complaining, then "Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum." and transfer.
252	[00:22:50] Burcu Tan: In the call center they also try a few times before escalating. Three is reasonable.
253	[00:22:55] Elçin Ural: Fine for me, as long as the assistant doesn't argue and doesn't answer insults.
254	[00:23:00] Ozan Er: No, never. It doesn't react to the insult. Only calming replies, and if the customer asks for an agent directly, we transfer right away, that's separate.
255	[00:23:07] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. Agent request is always immediate. Okay, three calming replies. Selin, can you change it?
256	[00:23:13] Selin Aydın: So we change what I said ten minutes ago [laughs]. Three calming replies, if the complaint continues, "Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum." and agent.
257	[00:23:21] Kerem Yalçın: Yes.
258	[00:23:22] Deniz Arı: Noted.
259	[00:23:24] Ozan Er: Can I double check the out-of-scope one, because of the agent topic? If someone asks something out of scope and also sounds angry, which one do we follow?
260	[00:23:31] Kerem Yalçın: Uh. Good question. If they're complaining, it's the complaint branch. If they just ask something unrelated, the out-of-scope question.
261	[00:23:38] Selin Aydın: And if they explicitly want an agent, agent. Without trying to convince them.
262	[00:23:42] Ozan Er: Okay, that's clear enough for us.
263	[00:23:45] Kerem Yalçın: Guys, I have a hard stop at three, so let's do a quick recap? Deniz?
264	[00:23:50] Deniz Arı: Sure, quickly, and I'll send it in writing too.
265	[00:23:53] Deniz Arı: Silence: first two times, short repeat of the question. Third time "Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum." and the call is closed.
266	[00:24:02] Deniz Arı: Unclear answer or refusal: ask again, three tries per question. After three: "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." Repeating information doesn't count.
267	[00:24:12] Deniz Arı: Non-Turkish: "Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum."
268	[00:24:15] Deniz Arı: Out of scope: "Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?" Yes, main menu. Continue, back to the flow. Unclear, ask again, three tries.
269	[00:24:26] Deniz Arı: Card selection: same name, last four. Same last four: "Son dört hanesi 4253 olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kartınızın son altı hanesini söyler misiniz?" Same last six: "Son altı hanesi aynı olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kart numaranızı söyler misiniz?"
270	[00:24:42] Selin Aydın: With the real digits, not 4253.
271	[00:24:44] Deniz Arı: Yes, of course, from the service.
272	[00:24:46] Deniz Arı: Angry customer: up to three calming replies, then "Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum." No reaction to insults.
273	[00:24:53] Deniz Arı: Currency names always in full, Türk Lirası, Dolar, Euro, İngiliz Sterlini, also in the no-debt sentence.
274	[00:25:00] Deniz Arı: Statement week: once per calendar year. Not offered if the right is used. Mentioning the limit is optional. Kerem checks the pre-check service with Mert.
275	[00:25:09] Deniz Arı: Joint statement: before the confirm question, "Bu değişiklik kartınıza bağlı [bağlı kart adı] kartınızı da etkileyecek." For the linked card holder, before the confirm question, that the main card is affected too.
276	[00:25:21] Deniz Arı: Normal end, nothing else wanted: "Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum." for now, to look at again with the routing project.
277	[00:25:28] Elçin Ural: One correction. For the joint statement, not only "before confirming". Before the question. I want the customer to hear it, and then the question comes.
278	[00:25:35] Deniz Arı: Yes, that's what I meant. Sentence first, then "Onaylıyor musunuz?".
279	[00:25:39] Elçin Ural: Okay.
280	[00:25:40] Kerem Yalçın: Good. Selin, you'll fix the document?
281	[00:25:43] Selin Aydın: I'll fix what I can by tomorrow. The edge case section I'll redo anyway, it's a mess.
282	[00:25:51] Deniz Arı: I'll send it, maybe not today, tomorrow or Friday.
283	[00:25:54] Selin Aydın: Fine.
284	[00:25:55] Burcu Tan: And I'll send the silence timing from the IVR. And I'll fix my prompts for the yearly limit, but that's for the IVR, not for you.
285	[00:26:02] Ozan Er: Thanks Burcu.
286	[00:26:04] Kerem Yalçın: Anything else? The [inaudible] mobile app topic we do next week, not today.
287	[00:26:09] Selin Aydın: Next week, yes. Ah, and Elçin, mandatory texts, is there anything the assistant must say at the start?
288	[00:26:15] Elçin Ural: I'm checking. I'll write to you. I don't think so for this flow because the customer is already identified in the IVR, but let me confirm.
289	[00:26:22] Selin Aydın: Okay, thanks.
290	[00:26:24] Deniz Arı: One more for us, sorry, thirty seconds. When the debt service doesn't answer, an error, we go to an agent, not main menu. Still okay?
291	[00:26:31] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. Service error, agent. The customer did nothing wrong, they shouldn't land in the menu.
292	[00:26:36] Deniz Arı: And the sentence from the mails stays, "Şu anda işleminizi gerçekleştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum."
293	[00:26:42] Kerem Yalçın: Yes.
294	[00:26:43] Deniz Arı: Perfect, that's all from us.
295	[00:26:45] Ozan Er: Oh, last thing, the digits. When the customer says "kırk iki elli üç" for the last four, that's the same as "dört iki beş üç", we just map it, we don't read it back.
296	[00:26:53] Selin Aydın: Yes, any way they say it.
297	[00:26:55] Kerem Yalçın: Okay, I really have to go. Thanks everyone, good session.
298	[00:26:58] Burcu Tan: Bye bye.
299	[00:26:59] Elçin Ural: Thanks, bye.
300	[00:27:00] Selin Aydın: Bye. Deniz, Ozan, can you stay one minute?
301	[00:27:03] Deniz Arı: Sure.
302	[00:27:05] Selin Aydın: Is it okay for you if the document only catches up next week? I have the quarterly report this week and honestly...
303	[00:27:11] Deniz Arı: No problem. We have our notes from today.
304	[00:27:15] Selin Aydın: Thanks. And the six-digit comment, you'll put it?
305	[00:27:18] Deniz Arı: Yes, right after this.
306	[00:27:20] Ozan Er: Selin, one question about the test cards, the two Yıldız cards in the test data, do they really share the last four?
307	[00:27:26] Selin Aydın: I think so, Mert built them for exactly that. Ask him, I'm not a hundred percent sure.
308	[00:27:31] Ozan Er: Okay, I'll ask.
309	[00:27:32] Selin Aydın: Okay. Thanks both. Talk Friday.
310	[00:27:34] Deniz Arı: Thanks, bye.
311	
312	[recording stopped]

[00:01:24] Ozan Er: Hi. Sorry, my camera is off, the internet here is a bit weak today.
[00:01:28] Burcu Tan: Are you at the office?
[00:01:29] Ozan Er: No, at home, the building is doing something with the cables. Since Monday.
[00:01:33] Burcu Tan: Ours was like that last year, three weeks. Good luck.
[00:01:36] Selin Aydın: Okay. While we wait for Kerem, maybe two small things on the reading part? Those don't need him.
[00:01:42] Deniz Arı: Sure. We had a few small ones too.
[00:01:45] Selin Aydın: First, the order. When a card has debt in more than one currency. I wrote Türk Lirası first, then the foreign currencies. Is that clear enough in the document?
[00:01:54] Ozan Er: Mostly. We read it as: the card intro with the statement date, then Türk Lirası, then Dolar, Euro, İngiliz Sterlini in that order, then one sentence for all the currencies with no debt, then the due date.
[00:02:06] Selin Aydın: Yes, exactly that.
[00:02:08] Ozan Er: And the remaining automatic payment, if there is one, before the due date.
[00:02:12] Selin Aydın: Yes. Before the due date.
[00:02:14] Burcu Tan: The IVR reads the due date last too. People remember the last thing they hear.
[00:02:18] Deniz Arı: Makes sense.
[00:02:20] Ozan Er: Then for the due date the sentence is "Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz [son ödeme tarihi]'dir." with the date like "21 Ekim 2025". Day, month name, year.
[00:02:30] Selin Aydın: Yes. And if the due date is today, it should say today. Not the date.
[00:02:35] Ozan Er: "Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz bugündür." Okay, we have that.
[00:02:39] Selin Aydın: Good.
[00:02:41] Deniz Arı: Second small one from us. After the debt is read, if the customer has more than one card, what comes first, the other-card question or the offer? E-mail and the week change.
[00:02:51] Selin Aydın: Hm. I'd say other card first. The customer called for the debt. If they have another card, maybe they want that one too.
[00:02:58] Deniz Arı: So: "Başka bir kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek ister misiniz?" and only when the cards are done, or they say no, the offer.
[00:03:05] Selin Aydın: Yes. Let's confirm with Kerem but I think he'll agree.
[00:03:09] Burcu Tan: And if they have only one card, you don't ask the other-card question, obviously.
[00:03:13] Deniz Arı: No, then straight to the offer.
[00:03:15] Ozan Er: And the offer only has what the customer can actually do. That's why we keep asking about the e-mail and the yearly right, it's connected.
[00:03:21] Selin Aydın: Yes, we'll get to that, it's in the yellow list.
[00:03:24] Ozan Er: Okay.
[00:03:26] Deniz Arı: The amounts, that's clear, I think. Lira and kuruş in full, like "bin iki yüz lira elli kuruş", and if kuruş is zero we don't say "sıfır kuruş".
[00:03:35] Selin Aydın: Yes. And the foreign currencies with cents. Sterlin with pence, um, "peni".
[00:03:40] Ozan Er: Yes, we did that already.
[00:03:42] Burcu Tan: Can I ask something off topic, sorry. Selin, the training on Thursday, is it still on?
[00:03:47] Selin Aydın: Which one? The onboarding group?
[00:03:49] Burcu Tan: The onboarding group, yes. I have two people starting.
[00:03:52] Selin Aydın: I think so. I'll check and write you.
[00:03:54] Burcu Tan: Thanks.
[00:03:56] Ozan Er: One more on the card question. The example card names in "Hangi kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek istersiniz? Örneğin, [kart adı] veya [kart adı] diyebilirsiniz." Those are the customer's own cards, max two, right?
[00:04:07] Selin Aydın: Yes. Never a card the customer doesn't have. It would confuse them.
[00:04:11] Ozan Er: Okay.
[00:04:12] Deniz Arı: And after the customer picks the card, we go to the debt. No "okay, continuing with your Yıldız card" sentence.
[00:04:18] Selin Aydın: No, that's not needed. The card name is in the first sentence of the reading anyway.
[00:04:23] Deniz Arı: Exactly.
[00:04:24] Selin Aydın: Okay. Let me open the edge cases, so we're ready when Kerem joins. Let me just... the sharing is not... one second.
[00:04:31] Burcu Tan: We see your mail.
[00:04:33] Selin Aydın: Oops. Okay. Now?
[00:04:35] Burcu Tan: Now a white page.
[00:04:37] Selin Aydın: It's loading. The file is big.
[00:04:40] Ozan Er: [inaudible] ...every time.
[00:04:43] Selin Aydın: Sorry?
[00:04:44] Ozan Er: Nothing, I said the same happens to me every time with that tool.
[00:04:48] Selin Aydın: [laughs] Okay. I'll stop sharing until Kerem is in.

[...]

[00:06:41] Kerem Yalçın: ...no, it's fine, the other meeting ran late, sorry. Can everyone hear me?
[00:06:44] Deniz Arı: Yes, loud and clear.

# Workflow format

This page describes the workflow JSON that defines a Freya agent. Read it before you write a builder. Tools, API calls and code are in [tools-and-code.md](tools-and-code.md). The REST calls are in [api.md](api.md).

Some statements are marked "verified in a working builder". Those come from a builder that created a 6-node workflow through the REST API and whose agent passed its practice cases.

## What a workflow is

A workflow describes a conversation as a graph. Each **node** is one step of the conversation and has its own prompt. **Transitions** move the conversation from one node to the next. A transition fires on what the user said or on the value of a variable.

When you create a workflow through the API, the platform creates an agent for it. You run simulations against that agent.

## Three model calls per turn

After each user message the platform makes three separate model calls. They do not share a prompt.

```text
user message
    |
    v
1. EXTRACTION   reads the message, stores variables
2. ROUTING      decides whether to leave the node
3. DIALOGUE     writes the agent's reply
```

| Call | What it sees | What it produces |
|---|---|---|
| Extraction | Recent conversation messages and the current node's `extraction_schema` | Variable values |
| Routing | Recent conversation messages and the transition descriptions. It does not see the dialogue prompt | The transition to take, or none |
| Dialogue | `system_prompt`, `role_message`, `task_message`, the full conversation history, and the node's `tools` | The reply, or a tool call |

Consequences:

- A routing instruction inside `task_message` has no effect on routing. Routing reads only transitions.
- The dialogue model can call only the tools in the current node's `tools` array. Everything else (API calls on entry, code, ending the call) is run by the workflow engine.
- Deterministic conditions (variable checks) need no model call. They are evaluated in code.

## Top-level keys

```json
{
  "initial_node": "greeting",
  "system_prompt": "You are the assistant of a dental clinic. Speak English.",
  "nodes": {},
  "global_nodes": {},
  "test_variables": { "customer_id": "c_test" }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `initial_node` | string | yes | Key of the node where every call starts |
| `nodes` | object | yes | Map of node key to node definition |
| `system_prompt` | string | no | Global rules. Part of the dialogue prompt in every node |
| `global_nodes` | object | no | Interrupt handlers that can fire from any node. See "Global nodes" |
| `test_variables` | object | no | Default values for call variables. See "Variables" |
| `context_variables` | object | no | A state block of chosen variables for the dialogue model. See "Context variables" |
| `tools` | array | no | Workflow-level lifecycle tools. See tools-and-code.md |
| `agent_config` | object | no | Model and call settings. See below |
| `nodePositions` | object | no | Layout for the visual editor. The working builder omits it |

**`agent_config`**: omit it. The platform fills in defaults. It holds model, voice and timeout settings that a builder for this event does not need. In a simulation you choose the models with the override fields described in api.md.

**No `null` values.** The schema is strict. Leave an optional field out, or set an optional string to `""`. A `null` fails validation.

The REST API takes the workflow inside a request body `{"name": "...", "workflow": {...}}`. The object described on this page is the value of `workflow`.

## Node types

| `node_type` | Purpose | Speaks to the user | Carries |
|---|---|---|---|
| `conversation` | A dialogue step | yes | `task_message`, `tools`, `extraction_schema`, `transitions` |
| `api_request` | Runs an HTTP call on entry | usually not | `pre_actions`, node-level `response_mapping`, `transitions` |
| `code` | Runs a Python snippet on entry | usually not | `pre_actions` with a `code_exec` function, `transitions` |
| `end_call` | Ends the call | optional farewell | `terminal` |

Other node types exist: `transfer_call`, `integration`, `knowledge_base`, `reschedule_call`, `invoke_agent`, `exit`. Telephony, voice settings, knowledge base and integrations also exist on the platform. You do not need any of them here and this page does not describe them.

The platform strips fields that do not belong to a node type, without an error:

- `tools` is kept only on `conversation` nodes.
- `pre_actions` is kept only on `api_request` and `code` nodes (and the other non-conversation action types).

So a node cannot have both. If a call must run before a conversation node, put it in its own `api_request` node in front.

## Node fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | | Node name. Use the same value as the node's key, in `snake_case` |
| `node_type` | string | | One of the types above |
| `task_message` | string | | The instruction for the dialogue model in this node |
| `role_message` | string | | Extra persona text for this node. Rarely needed |
| `on_enter` | object | `{"type": "llm"}` | What happens on entry. See "Entry behaviour" |
| `on_enter_first_entry_only` | boolean | `false` | Run the entry behaviour only on the first visit |
| `transitions` | array | | Outgoing transitions, in priority order |
| `routing_prompt` | string | | Extra context for the routing model in this node |
| `loop_condition` | string | | Intent description for staying in the node. See "Loop conditions" |
| `loop_prompt` | string | | Replaces `task_message` from the second turn in the node |
| `extraction_schema` | array | | Variables to extract from user speech in this node |
| `tools` | array | | Tools the dialogue model may call. `conversation` nodes only |
| `pre_actions` | array | | Calls the engine runs on entry. `api_request` and `code` nodes |
| `response_mapping` | array | | For `pre_actions` nodes: maps the call result to variables. Node level |
| `passthrough` | boolean | `false` | Route right after entry, without waiting for the user |
| `passthrough_default_transition` | string | | Target node for a passthrough node |
| `max_node_turns` | integer | `10` | Cap on user turns spent in the node |
| `max_turn_transition` | string | | Target node when the cap is reached |
| `terminal` | object | | The end-call function. `end_call` nodes only |
| `disable_inactivity_monitor` | boolean | `false` | Switch off silence check-ins for this node |
| `suppress_tool_results` | boolean | `false` | Hide raw call results from the dialogue model. See tools-and-code.md |
| `truncation_strategy` | string | `keep_all` | How much history the dialogue model sees. See "Limits" |
| `truncation_window_size` | integer | `10` | Number of recent messages kept by `keep_recent` and `summarize` |
| `reasoning_override` | string | `auto` | `enabled` or `disabled` forces model reasoning on or off for this node. Only models that support such a switch react to it |

A per-node `idle_config` (silence timeouts) and per-node speech settings also exist. They matter on voice calls only.

## Prompts

The dialogue model receives one system message built from three parts:

```text
system_prompt        workflow level, the same in every node
role_message         node level, optional
## Current Task
task_message         node level, what to do now
```

| Field | Level | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `system_prompt` | workflow | Identity, language, tone, rules that hold in every node |
| `role_message` | node | A different persona for one node. Most workflows leave it out |
| `task_message` | node | What the agent must do in this step |
| `loop_prompt` | node | A replacement for `task_message` after the first turn in the node |
| `on_enter` | node | What the agent does when it enters the node |

Rules for `task_message`:

- Write instructions for the model, not a script.
- Cover this node's job only.
- Do not describe routing or name other nodes. The model does not know about nodes. Text such as "then move to the lookup node" makes it narrate steps that have not happened.
- If the node has tools, refer to them by name and say when to call them. Do not repeat the tool descriptions.
- In a node without tools, state that no tool call is allowed in this turn. If the node has a `loop_prompt`, put that rule in both prompts.

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "collect_details",
  "node_type": "conversation",
  "task_message": "Ask which service the caller wants and on which day. Ask one question at a time. If the caller is unsure about the day, offer to check the next free days.",
  "transitions": []
}
```

### Entry behaviour

| `on_enter` | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `{"type": "llm"}` | The model writes the first line from `task_message`. Default. An optional `prompt` key overrides the entry instruction for this node |
| `{"type": "tts", "text": "..."}` | A fixed line is spoken. No model call. `{{var}}` works in `text` |
| `{"type": "silent"}` | Nothing is said. The node waits for the user, or routes at once if it is a passthrough node |
| `{"type": "audio", "asset_id": "..."}` | Plays a recorded asset. Not needed here |

Set `on_enter_first_entry_only` to `true` when a node can be re-entered and must not repeat its opening line. This works better than a prompt rule such as "do not greet twice".

### History across nodes

When the conversation moves from node A to node B:

- User and assistant messages are kept.
- The system message is replaced by node B's prompts.
- A loop prompt from node A is removed.

So node B can refer to anything said earlier. Variables also stay for the whole call.

## Variables

All variables live in one table for the whole call. There is no per-node scope. A variable is never cleared on a transition. A later write with the same name overwrites it.

| Source | How it gets in |
|---|---|
| Call variables | Passed when the call or simulation starts |
| `test_variables` | Workflow-level defaults for call variables |
| Extraction | `extraction_schema` on a node |
| Call results | `response_mapping`, and the automatic result keys described in tools-and-code.md |
| Code | A code node or `code_exec` tool writes into `vars` |
| System | Set by the platform |

### `{{var}}` substitution

Write `{{variable_name}}` in prompts, `on_enter.text`, transition descriptions, URLs, headers and request bodies. The engine replaces it before the model or the HTTP call sees the text.

| Form | Result |
|---|---|
| `{{customer_name}}` | The value as a string |
| `{{amount:json}}` | The value JSON-encoded. Use it inside request bodies |

Behaviour to know:

- Date values are formatted for speech in the agent's language when they are substituted into a prompt.
- An unresolved variable in a prompt stays as the literal text `{{variable_name}}`. The model sees the placeholder. In a fixed spoken line (`on_enter.text`, a terminal `spoken_message`) the agent says it aloud.
- In a field of an engine-run call (a `pre_actions` call or a lifecycle tool) an unresolved placeholder behaves in two ways. If the value is exactly one placeholder (`"{{x}}"`), the whole field is dropped from the request. If the value mixes text and a placeholder (`"Status: {{x}}"`), the request goes out with the literal `{{x}}` in it.
- Do not reference a variable in a mixed value unless an earlier node always sets it.

### Call variables and `test_variables`

Call variables are the inputs of one call, for example a customer id or the current time. In a simulation you pass them per persona in `customerVariablesMap` (see api.md).

`test_variables` is a top-level object of default values. On a web call to the workflow it is merged into the call variables. A value passed with the call wins over a test variable of the same name.

```json
{
  "test_variables": {
    "customer_id": "c_test",
    "first_name": "Dana",
    "now": "2026-03-11T10:00"
  }
}
```

Verified in a working builder: call variables are readable as `{{customer_id}}` in prompts and tool parameters, and as `vars.get("customer_id")` in code.

### System variables

| Variable | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `{{system.iso_utc_now}}` | `2026-03-11T14:30:00Z` | UTC timestamp of call start |
| `{{system.todays_date_en_cst}}` | `11 March 2026 Wednesday 08:30` | English date, UTC-6 |
| `{{system.todays_date_en_est}}` | `11 March 2026 Wednesday 09:30` | English date, UTC-5 |
| `{{system.todays_date_tr}}` | | Turkish date with day name and time, UTC+3 |
| `{{system.todays_date_tr.iso_8601}}` | `2026-03-11` | ISO date, UTC+3 |
| `{{system.conversation}}` | `AGENT: hello\nUSER: hi` | Transcript so far |
| `{{system.conversation.last-N}}` | | Last N turns. N is `1`, `5`, `10` or `20` |
| `{{call.direction}}` | `web` | `inbound`, `outbound`, `web` or `simulation`. A chat simulation in the trial showed `web` |
| `{{call.duration}}` | `42` | Whole seconds since call start |
| `{{call.call_id}}` | | Platform call id |
| `{{<node>.current_turns}}` | `2` | User turns in the node since the last entry. Resets on every transition |
| `{{<node>.total_turns}}` | `5` | User turns in the node over the whole call |

There is no `{{current_date}}` placeholder. These system dates are the real clock. If your task supplies its own "now" as a call variable, use that variable.

`{{system.conversation.last-N}}` is useful in a transition description or a `routing_prompt` when the routing model needs more than the last message.

### Context variables

Warning from a test on 10 October: a workflow saved over the API came back without this key, and the save gave no error. Do not rely on it. Write the values the model needs into the prompt with `{{variable}}` instead.

`context_variables` is a top-level key. It shows chosen variables to the dialogue model as a state block, so you do not have to write variable tables into prompt text.

```json
{
  "context_variables": {
    "pre_history_description": "Static call context",
    "post_history_description": "Live state",
    "items": [
      { "name": "customer_tier", "placement": "pre_history", "description": "Customer tier" },
      { "name": "attempt_count", "placement": "post_history" }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `items[].name` | Name of a variable in the variable table. Must match `^[a-zA-Z_]\w*$` and be unique across both placements |
| `items[].placement` | `pre_history` or `post_history` |
| `items[].description` | Optional label |
| `pre_history_description`, `post_history_description` | Heading text of each section |

Rules:

- An item points at a variable. It does not create one. If nothing sets the variable, the row is skipped without an error.
- `pre_history` is written once into the system prompt. Use it only for values that never change during the call.
- `post_history` is rendered again on every turn after the chat history and is not stored in the history. Use it for values that change.
- The block is rendered as `<CONTEXT_VARIABLES>`, one line `- name (description): value` per populated item.
- No other keys are allowed on an item. There is no `value`, `type` or `default`.
- It does not affect extraction or tool parameter substitution.

## Transitions

A transition is an object in a node's `transitions` array.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `target_node` | string | Key of the next node. May be the node itself. `__previous__` is allowed in global nodes |
| `description` | string | What the transition is for. The routing model reads it |
| `condition` | object | When the transition fires |
| `is_tool_call` | boolean | The dialogue model triggers the transition by calling a tool. See "Tool-call transitions" |

### Condition operators

Deterministic operators check a variable in code. No model call.

| Operator | Needs | True when |
|---|---|---|
| `equals` | `variable`, `operand` | `str(value) == str(operand)` |
| `not_equals` | `variable`, `operand` | The inverse of `equals` |
| `greater_than` | `variable`, `operand` | `float(value) > float(operand)` |
| `less_than` | `variable`, `operand` | `float(value) < float(operand)` |
| `contains` | `variable`, `operand` | `operand` is a substring of the value, ignoring case |
| `is_set` | `variable` | The variable has any value |
| `is_not_set` | `variable` | The variable has no value |
| `always` | nothing | Always |

The semantic operator uses the routing model.

| Operator | Needs | True when |
|---|---|---|
| `matches_intent` | `description` | The routing model judges that the user's last message matches the description |

All `matches_intent` conditions of one evaluation are judged in a single model call.

### Condition shapes

An unconditional transition:

```json
{ "target_node": "next_step", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
```

An intent condition:

```json
{
  "target_node": "complaint",
  "description": "The user wants to complain",
  "condition": { "operator": "matches_intent", "description": "The user is unhappy or wants to file a complaint" }
}
```

Variable conditions go inside a group. The top-level group always uses `"logic": "or"`:

```json
{
  "target_node": "order_found",
  "description": "The lookup returned an order",
  "condition": {
    "logic": "or",
    "conditions": [
      { "variable": "order_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "shipped" },
      { "variable": "order_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "delivered" }
    ]
  }
}
```

For AND, nest a group inside the top-level OR. Never put `"logic": "and"` at the top level.

```json
{
  "target_node": "priority_desk",
  "description": "Gold customer with a late order",
  "condition": {
    "logic": "or",
    "conditions": [
      {
        "logic": "and",
        "conditions": [
          { "variable": "customer_tier", "operator": "equals", "operand": "gold" },
          { "variable": "days_late", "operator": "greater_than", "operand": 3 }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The working builder uses the bare form for `always` and the grouped form for every variable check. The internal reference also shows a bare single variable condition (`{"variable": ..., "operator": ..., "operand": ...}`) directly under `condition`.

### Do not route on a boolean

`equals` compares strings. A boolean can arrive as `"True"` or as `"true"`, depending on how it was written into the table. A mismatch fails silently: the branch never fires and nothing reports an error.

- Prefer a string value such as `verified` or `rejected`, written by your code or by the API.
- If you must test a boolean that comes from an API response, test both spellings. Verified in a working builder:

```json
{
  "target_node": "wrap_up",
  "description": "The booking call succeeded",
  "condition": {
    "logic": "or",
    "conditions": [
      { "variable": "booking_ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
      { "variable": "booking_ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" }
    ]
  }
}
```

`greater_than` and `less_than` convert both sides to numbers, so `2` and `"2"` behave the same. Use them for counters.

### Order of evaluation

After each user message, routing runs in this order. The first match wins and routing stops.

```text
1. loop_condition of the current node    match: stay in the node, use loop_prompt
2. the node's transitions, in list order match: go to target_node
3. global nodes                          match: enter the global node
4. nothing matched                       stay in the node, wait for the next user message
```

Within step 2:

- Transitions are checked in list order. Put specific conditions first and broad ones last.
- Deterministic conditions are evaluated first. If one matches, no routing model call is made.
- If several transitions of a node have the same `target_node`, the engine merges them at load time into one transition. Its condition is the OR of the originals. If one of them is unconditional, the merged transition is unconditional.

Routing also runs after a tool result arrives. Verified in a working builder: a transition on a variable that a tool's `response_mapping` sets fires in the same turn, without a further user message.

When nothing matches, there is no fallback. The agent stays and answers from the same `task_message`. Make sure every realistic path has a matching transition.

### `routing_prompt`

A node-level string. It replaces the default intent-matching instruction of the routing model for this node. Use it when the transition descriptions cannot carry the rule, for example "stay here until both the name and the date are given".

### Self-transition

A last transition with `always` that targets the node itself keeps the user in the node until an earlier transition matches.

```json
{ "target_node": "collect_details", "description": "Keep collecting", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
```

Prefer this to `loop_condition` in most cases. All routing then lives in one ordered list.

### Loop conditions

`loop_condition` is an intent description. The routing model checks it before all transitions. When it matches, the agent stays in the node.

`loop_prompt` replaces `task_message` in the system message from the second turn in the node. The model sees one of the two, never both. Write it so that it stands alone. `{{var}}` works in it, so it can show what was already collected.

```json
{
  "name": "collect_contact",
  "node_type": "conversation",
  "task_message": "Ask for the caller's full name and email address.",
  "loop_condition": "The user has not yet given both a full name and an email address",
  "loop_prompt": "Name so far: {{customer_name}}. Email so far: {{email}}. Ask only for what is still missing. When both are present, read them back once.",
  "transitions": []
}
```

Make the loop condition specific. "The user has not finished" matches everything and the agent never leaves.

### Tool-call transitions

Set `is_tool_call` to `true` on a transition. The dialogue model then sees the transition as a tool named `transition_to_<node>` and triggers it by calling that tool. The router does not evaluate it after each turn.

```json
{
  "target_node": "confirm_booking",
  "description": "The caller accepted the offered slot",
  "is_tool_call": true,
  "condition": { "operator": "matches_intent", "description": "The caller accepted the offered slot" }
}
```

Use it when the agent should decide to move, for example because of something it just said or computed. The agent can acknowledge and move in the same message. The target node's `on_enter` then asks the next question. Global nodes accept the same flag.

### Passthrough nodes

A node with `"passthrough": true` routes right after its entry actions. It does not wait for the user. `api_request` and `code` nodes are normally passthrough nodes.

- Set `passthrough_default_transition` to the next node.
- End `transitions` with an `always` transition. A passthrough node with no matching transition deadlocks.
- Set `on_enter` to `{"type": "silent"}`, or to a short fixed line that covers the wait.

```json
{
  "name": "prepare",
  "node_type": "code",
  "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "greeting",
  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
  "pre_actions": [],
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "greeting", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

Verified in a working builder: a passthrough `code` node can be the `initial_node`. It runs before the agent says anything.

### Global nodes

A global node is an interrupt handler. It can fire from any node. It is checked only after the current node's own transitions found no match.

A global node has the same fields as a normal node, plus:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `condition` | When the global node activates. Same format as a transition condition |
| `description` | Purpose of the node |
| `excluded_nodes` | Array of node keys where it must not fire |
| `is_tool_call` | Offer the global node to the dialogue model as a tool, not as a per-turn check |

`__previous__` as a `target_node` or as `passthrough_default_transition` returns to the node that was interrupted.

```json
{
  "global_nodes": {
    "off_topic": {
      "name": "off_topic",
      "description": "Brings the caller back to the subject",
      "condition": { "operator": "matches_intent", "description": "The user talks about something unrelated to their order" },
      "task_message": "Redirect the caller to the subject.",
      "on_enter": { "type": "tts", "text": "I can only help with your order. Let us continue." },
      "passthrough": true,
      "passthrough_default_transition": "__previous__",
      "excluded_nodes": ["goodbye"],
      "transitions": [
        { "target_node": "__previous__", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Rules:

- List terminal nodes in `excluded_nodes`, or the global node can loop.
- Exclude nodes where an interrupt would do harm, for example an identity check.
- For a plain redirect use a passthrough node with a fixed line. It is faster and more predictable than a model reply.
- Use global nodes for interrupts that can happen anywhere. Do not copy the same transition into every node.

## Extraction schema

`extraction_schema` is an array on a node. After each user message the extraction model fills the listed variables from the conversation.

```json
{
  "extraction_schema": [
    {
      "name": "order_number",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The order number the caller reads out",
      "validation_pattern": "^[0-9]{8}$",
      "max_retries": 2,
      "min_confidence": 0.8
    },
    {
      "name": "request_type",
      "type": "string",
      "enum_values": ["status", "cancel", "change_address", "other"],
      "description": "What the caller wants to do with the order",
      "min_confidence": 0.7
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Variable name |
| `type` | string | `string`, `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `name`, `phone_number` |
| `description` | string | What the variable is |
| `enum_values` | array | Allowed values. Works on every type. The old `enum` type is deprecated and becomes `string` |
| `extraction_prompt` | string | A custom extraction template. See the warning below |
| `validation_pattern` | string | Regular expression the value must match |
| `min_confidence` | number | 0.0 to 1.0. Values below it are discarded. Default `0.95` |
| `max_retries` | integer | Retries after a failed validation, with the error given to the model |

How it works:

1. The extraction model sees recent messages and the schema.
2. It returns structured values.
3. Confidence is computed from the model's token probabilities, not from a self-report.
4. Each value is checked against `validation_pattern` and `enum_values`.
5. On failure the model retries, up to `max_retries`.

Rules:

- **Set `min_confidence` on every variable.** The default of 0.95 is strict. A discarded value leaves no trace in the transcript, so it looks the same as "nothing was extracted".
- **`extraction_prompt` replaces the whole built-in template.** It is not appended. A custom prompt must contain the input placeholders itself: `{{extractor.speech}}`, `{{extractor.conversation.last-10}}`, `{{extractor.type_preamble}}` and `{{extractor.variables_list}}`. Without them the extractor never sees the user's message and returns nothing on every turn, while dialogue and routing look healthy.
- **Declare dates as `type: "date"`.** The date types give the extractor today's date and the rules for relative dates such as "tomorrow". A date typed as `string` gets no date anchor and the model guesses the year.
- The built-in date rules turn vague expressions such as "next week" into a concrete date. If you need vague dates rejected, a custom prompt must say so and state that this overrides the general rules.
- No `null`. Omit optional fields or use `""`.
- An extracted variable is available to the same node's transitions in the same turn, and to every later node.

Inside `extraction_prompt` these date placeholders resolve: `{{date.today}}`, `{{time.now}}`, `{{date.day_of_week}}`, `{{date.yesterday}}`, `{{date.tomorrow}}`, `{{date.day_after_tomorrow}}`, `{{date.next_week}}`, `{{date.end_of_month}}`, `{{date.first_next_month}}`, `{{date.next_mon}}` to `{{date.next_sun}}`, `{{date.last_mon}}` to `{{date.last_sun}}`, `{{date.fnm_mon}}` to `{{date.fnm_sun}}` (first such weekday of next month), `{{date.weeks2}}`, `{{date.weeks3}}`, `{{date.weeks2_ago}}`, `{{date.weeks3_ago}}`. Do not rely on them outside extraction prompts.

**Fork on an extracted enum.** To route from one node to several paths, extract an enum and branch with `equals`. This is more reliable than several competing `matches_intent` transitions.

```json
{
  "name": "menu",
  "node_type": "conversation",
  "task_message": "Tell the caller the order status in one sentence. Then ask whether they want to change the delivery address, cancel the order, or end the call.",
  "extraction_schema": [
    {
      "name": "next_action",
      "type": "string",
      "enum_values": ["change_address", "cancel", "done"],
      "description": "What the caller chose. Empty if unclear.",
      "min_confidence": 0.7
    }
  ],
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "change_address", "description": "Change address", "condition": { "logic": "or", "conditions": [ { "variable": "next_action", "operator": "equals", "operand": "change_address" } ] } },
    { "target_node": "cancel_order", "description": "Cancel", "condition": { "logic": "or", "conditions": [ { "variable": "next_action", "operator": "equals", "operand": "cancel" } ] } },
    { "target_node": "goodbye", "description": "Done", "condition": { "logic": "or", "conditions": [ { "variable": "next_action", "operator": "equals", "operand": "done" } ] } },
